```plato
//==
// # Intrinsics — the host contract
//
// An **intrinsic** is a function the language declares but does not define: a
// signature terminated by `;` with no `=>` body, inside a `library` block. The
// host runtime supplies the implementation. This file is the complete contract a
// backend must satisfy — for C# that is the handwritten `Plato.Intrinsics`;
// for a new backend (C++, GLSL, Rust) it is the porting checklist.
//
// **Rule: a bodiless intrinsic may mention only `primitive` types** (Number,
// Integer, Boolean, Character, String, Array, Buffer, List, Function0-9,
// Type — see `primitives.plato`).
//
// **Admission rule (plato-378): an intrinsic must not be expressible in Plato
// from the other intrinsics.** If a portable reference body exists, the function
// belongs in a `*.library.plato` file and the backend recovers native speed
// through its override table (plato-368), not by growing this list. Everything
// on Angle, Number2/3/4/8, Vector2D/3D, Matrix3x2/4x4 and Quaternion left under
// that rule; the array reshaping family and the derivable scalar surface
// followed it. `IntrinsicsSurfaceTests` pins the count so the list cannot drift
// back up.
//
// Target backends, in priority order: C#, C++, CUDA, TypeScript, then GLSL, Rust,
// Python (see README.md "Target backends"). An intrinsic belongs here only if every
// priority-1..4 target can supply it natively or with a trivial shim; anything
// C#-specific stays out (see the notes at the bottom of this file).
//
// Bodiless declarations inside a `interface` are NOT intrinsics — those are
// obligations on whoever implements the interface, and the stdlib satisfies them in
// Plato. Only `library` blocks declare host intrinsics.
//
// This is the ONLY file in the library with bodiless declarations, and it stays
// that way.

library Intrinsics
{
    //==
    // Number — the irreducible scalar kernel.
    //
    // Everything derivable from these has a reference body in
    // `primitives.library.plato`: Abs, Sign, Square, Reciprocal, Min,
    // Max, Ceiling, Truncate, Log/Log2/Log10, the Tan/Cosh/Sinh/Tanh
    // family, the whole inverse-trig family (over Atan2Radians and NaturalLog),
    // Zero/One/Tau/E, IsFinite, and the five relational operators the IOrderable
    // generics already cover.

    Add(a: Number, b: Number): Number;
    Subtract(a: Number, b: Number): Number;
    Multiply(a: Number, b: Number): Number;
    Divide(a: Number, b: Number): Number;
    Modulo(a: Number, b: Number): Number;
    Negative(n: Number): Number;

    // The total order and structural equality. LessThanOrEquals is the single
    // IOrderable primitive; LessThan / GreaterThan / GreaterThanOrEquals /
    // Compare / Clamp / Lesser / Greater all derive from it in
    // `core.library.plato`, and NotEquals from Equals.
    LessThanOrEquals(a: Number, b: Number): Boolean;
    Equals(a: Number, b: Number): Boolean;

    // Bit-level digest: not expressible over arithmetic.
    Hash(self: Number): Integer;

    // Rounding: Floor is the primitive, Ceiling and Truncate derive from it.
    // Round carries a digit count because decimal scaling loses precision when
    // synthesized from Floor.
    Floor(self: Number): Number;
    Round(self: Number, digits: Integer): Number;

    // Transcendental kernel. Pow stays a primitive because Exp(y * Log x) is
    // wrong for a negative base; FusedMultiplyAdd stays because its single
    // rounding is a SEMANTIC difference from a * b + c, not an optimization.
    Sqrt(self: Number): Number;
    // Correctly rounded real cube root (odd; a zero keeps its sign). Pow(x, 1/3) is not: it differs in the last bit.
    Cbrt(self: Number): Number;
    Exp(self: Number): Number;
    NaturalLog(self: Number): Number;
    Pow(self: Number, power: Number): Number;
    FusedMultiplyAdd(self: Number, y: Number, z: Number): Number;

    // Trigonometric kernel over radians-as-Number. The public trig surface lives
    // on Angle (angles.library.plato) with plain Plato bodies delegating
    // here. Sin, Cos and the two-argument arctangent are the whole kernel:
    // Tan/Cosh/Sinh/Tanh and the six inverse forms derive from these plus Exp
    // and NaturalLog.
    Sin(self: Number): Number;
    Cos(self: Number): Number;
    Atan2Radians(self: Number, x: Number): Number;

    // Representation limits and the one constant that is not a formula over
    // another. Tau = 2 Pi and E = Exp(1) are derived.
    MinValue(_: Number): Number;
    MaxValue(_: Number): Number;
    Epsilon(_: Number): Number;
    Pi(_: Number): Number;

    // Non-finite classification: IsFinite is derived from these two.
    IsNaN(self: Number): Boolean;
    IsInfinite(self: Number): Boolean;

    ToInteger(self: Number): Integer;

    //==
    // Integer
    //
    // Derived in `primitives.library.plato`: Abs, Sign, Min, Max,
    // Zero, One, Range, and the relational family.

    Add(a: Integer, b: Integer): Integer;
    Subtract(a: Integer, b: Integer): Integer;
    Multiply(a: Integer, b: Integer): Integer;
    Divide(a: Integer, b: Integer): Integer;
    Modulo(a: Integer, b: Integer): Integer;
    Negative(n: Integer): Integer;

    LessThanOrEquals(a: Integer, b: Integer): Boolean;
    Equals(a: Integer, b: Integer): Boolean;
    Hash(self: Integer): Integer;

    BitwiseAnd(a: Integer, b: Integer): Integer;
    BitwiseOr(a: Integer, b: Integer): Integer;
    BitwiseXor(a: Integer, b: Integer): Integer;
    BitwiseNot(x: Integer): Integer;
    ShiftLeft(x: Integer, bits: Integer): Integer;
    ShiftRight(x: Integer, bits: Integer): Integer;

    MinValue(_: Integer): Integer;
    MaxValue(_: Integer): Integer;

    ToNumber(self: Integer): Number;

    //==
    // Boolean
    //
    // The three connectives. Equals, ExclusiveOr, Compare and Hash are derived
    // in `primitives.library.plato`; LessThanOrEquals (false orders before
    // true) is derived there too.

    And(a: Boolean, b: Boolean): Boolean;
    Or(a: Boolean, b: Boolean): Boolean;
    Not(b: Boolean): Boolean;

    //==
    // Character and String
    //
    // Both primitives declare `IOrderable` (primitives.plato), which the host must
    // discharge: String order is ordinal in every runtime (UTF-16 code units in C#
    // and the interpreter, bytes in the C++ prelude; the same for ASCII), never the
    // platform's culture collation: "B" < "a", and a prefix precedes its extension.
    // Operator-named, so the C# writer synthesizes the wrapper from the runtime's
    // comparison operators.

    LessThanOrEquals(a: Character, b: Character): Boolean;
    LessThanOrEquals(a: String, b: String): Boolean;

    // The only constructor of a String that is not a literal: the characters of the
    // array in order, and the empty String for the empty array. Irreducible: a String
    // is opaque, so no composition of the observers (Count, At) can build one.
    // Witness: FromCharacters of the characters of "ab" is "ab"; of none, "".
    FromCharacters(cs: Array<Character>): String;
```
